title: Bastionless VPC Bootstrap and Conditional Mirror Upgrade Contract
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a bastionless bootstrap and staged upgrade flow for Private/VPC deployments where direct operator SSH or persistent bastion hosts are disallowed. The flow must support constrained egress (allowlist-only), intermittent mirror synchronization, and an operator-driven signed-artifact import path for fully air-gapped sites.
background: Multiple regulated customers and internal security reviews have requested removal of long-lived bastion hosts from private deployments. Operators must still be able to install, upgrade, and troubleshoot clusters without opening broad egress or relying on persistent jump servers. Current upgrade flows assume a reachable operator bastion or full internet egress for image pulls. This PRD defines a secure, verifiable alternative leveraging ephemeral operator sessions, signed artifact bundles, and conditional mirror policies.
goals: Enable cluster bootstrap and upgrades without persistent bastion hosts
Support customers with allowlist-based egress and fully offline (air-gapped) installations
Provide verifiable artifact provenance and automated sanity checks during upgrade
Offer operator UX that minimizes manual checklist steps while preserving security controls
non_goals: Replace all remote debugging workflows that require full interactive shells (we still support operator-side debugging via recorded sessions)
Remove the option for customer-managed bastions where teams explicitly require them
Provide automated failure resolution for arbitrary third-party OS-level issues unrelated to Redwood artifacts
assumptions: Customer can provide a small set of egress allowlist entries for staged mirror sync (if not fully air-gapped)
Operator machines have a trusted hardware or key storage mechanism for signing/verification workflows
Customers with fully air-gapped sites can deliver signed artifact bundles via removable media or internal registries
requirements: REQ-1: Bootstrap must succeed without a bastion by using an ephemeral operator-initiated handshake (signed token exchange)
REQ-2: Upgrade artifacts (images, helm charts, operators) must be cryptographically signed and verifiable offline
REQ-3: Mirror sync can be configured in three modes: full-online, staged-mirror-with-allowlist, and manual-bundle-import (air-gapped)
REQ-4: The control plane must provide a preflight verification step that validates checksums, signatures, and semantic compatibility before applying an upgrade
REQ-5: All network flows required for bootstrap/upgrade must be documented and expressible as a minimal allowlist (IP ranges/FQDNs and ports)
REQ-6: Rollouts must support canary increments at component-level with automated rollback triggers based on health and API latency SLOs
REQ-7: Telemetry and audit logs related to bootstrap/upgrade must be exported to the customer-managed logging endpoint or kept local per the deployment policy
REQ-8: Operator actions that could alter egress or add open inbound surfaces require a signed consent step recorded in the audit log
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A new empty VPC customer environment can be bootstrapped to a usable control plane without adding a bastion host when using the ephemeral handshake flow

AC-2: In staged-mirror-with-allowlist mode, the cluster successfully performs a mirror sync using only the documented allowlist within two sync windows (24 hours total) and reports checksums for all artifacts
AC-3: In manual-bundle-import mode, an operator can import a signed bundle (tarball) containing all required images and manifests and the platform verifies signatures and checksums before installing

AC-4: An upgrade test run completes in canary mode (10% of control-plane replicas) and the system auto-rolls back when a synthetic API latency test exceeds configured SLO by >= 30% for 3 consecutive minutes
AC-5: The upgrade preflight must detect mismatched kernel/architecture flags for at least three common host OSes and fail with actionable remediation steps
AC-6: All bootstrap/upgrade operations emit verifiable audit entries including operator identity (OIDC or signed token), operation timestamp, input bundle checksum, and decision outcome
AC-7: No persistent inbound ports are opened as part of bootstrap/upgrade in any supported mode (bastionless default). Any temporary inbound requirement must be explicitly consented and logged
AC-8: Security review validates that private keys used for signing bundles are never transmitted to the cluster during verification; only public keys or verification certificates are used
test_plan: TP-1: Fresh VPC lab: run full bootstrap in all three mirror modes and validate control plane readiness within 60 minutes (online), 90 minutes (staged mirror), and 180 minutes (manual bundle)
TP-2: Fault injection: simulate mirror sync interruption and verify resumability and idempotent artifact application
TP-3: Signature tampering: modify a single manifest in a bundle and assert that verification fails and install is blocked
TP-4: Canary health gating: run synthetic request load against canary and baseline and assert rollback triggers fire under degraded conditions
TP-5: Audit export: validate that audit entries are delivered to configured logging sinks or can be exported as a signed artifact for customer retention
rollout_plan: Rollout will start with internal alpha customers and Redwood engineering labs. Phase 1: dry-run in internal infra (2 weeks). Phase 2: invitation-only external customers with security review complete (4-6 weeks). Phase 3: general availability with docs and partner playbooks.
rollback_criteria: Rollback will be triggered automatically on canary SLA breaches, failed preflight validations post-deploy, or manual operator trigger. Rollback will restore previous bundle and re-run preflight. Operator must supply a postmortem within 48 hours when rollback occurs.
operator_runbook_summary: Ephemeral handshake: operator generates signed session token via customer OIDC + local HSM; customer cluster fetches bootstrap bundle from staged mirror or accepts manual bundle; verification runs; install starts. For air-gapped manual import, operator places signed bundle on node, runs 'redwoodctl import-bundle --verify', and monitors preflight logs.
network_allowlist_reference: Minimum egress: TLS outbound to mirrors.redwood.ai:443 (if staged mode) and allowlist of mirror IP ranges (provided per-region)
Optional: customer-managed registry endpoints (internal):443 and registry IP ranges
Ports: 443 outbound for image pulls; 22 only for optional operator SSH for on-prem tasks (must be disabled by default)
DNS: customer resolver access must be allowed for FQDN resolution during staged sync
dependencies: ENG-20102: mirror-scheduler that supports incremental sync and resumability
risks: R1: Customers with extremely restrictive allowlists may still refuse any outbound connectivity, increasing manual operator effort
R2: If signing key lifecycle is not well-managed by customers, verification may fail and block upgrades
R3: Increased support load for manual-bundle imports during GA period
mitigations: M1: Provide a low-friction operator wizard and checklist for manual import scenarios; pre-generate minimal allowlist templates
M2: Offer managed key escrow options and key rotation playbooks (customer opt-in)
M3: Early engagement with high-risk customers to script mirror sync windows and provide concierge import support
open_questions: Q1: Should we ship a customer-facing hardware-token signing utility or rely solely on third-party HSMs?
Q2: What SLAs will we commit to for mirror sync timeliness in staged-mirror mode?
Q3: How should we surface detailed preflight errors to non-engineer operators while preserving security context?
notes: This contract emphasizes verifiability and operator safety. Engineering should implement extensive unit tests around signature verification and preflight checks. UX should prioritize a single guided flow for manual-bundle import to reduce human error. Delivery owner: Miguel Torres.
